earlier_scan.source_named: Parrish, David. 1989. Bore grammar essentials. Madang: Pioneer Bible Translators. 131 pp. (grammar sketch; Glottolog ref 575864)
earlier_scan.note: Only substantive description of Borei/Bore; manuscript held by PBT/Glottolog, no online copy found. Otherwise just Z'graggen survey wordlists.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 1.3.3 p. 6; sec. 2.23.11 Ottilien Family pp. 74-76 (Gamei = language 49/Ga)
sources.note: Survey-wide, p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Gamei entry (p. 75) only refers to 'Capell (1952: 134ff) gives a first phoneme chart, some notes on grammar and a wordlist'; Ottilien typological characteristics (p. 76) list segmental features only, nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu Basin. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Watam-Awar-Gamay comparative wordlists and consonant correspondences (pp. 116-118), Gamay forms unmarked for stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Entry 144 Gamei.
sources.note: Nothing; villages and population, 'all data, except population, from Z'graggen (1971)'.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: Bore; Ramu Coast; Lower Ramu River (wiki pages, Santa Fe Institute)
sources.note: Nothing: Bore phonology section '[under construction]' beyond Parrish's segment inventory; Ramu Coast page has a '… stress …' placeholder with no content. Lists Bore sources: Capell 1951-52: 198-200 (80 terms), Z'graggen 1972 (406 terms), Parrish 1989 (grammar), Foley 2005: 116-118.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
